channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Year-round food production coming to Saskatchewan First Nation
item.description: Cowessess First Nation is planning to construct another sustainable project with the help of the federal government.

item.title: U.S. ethanol industry sets its sights on the world
item.description: Canada remains the top buyer of U.S. ethanol but Mexico and Japan have huge potential.

item.title: New U.S. tariffs start at 10 per cent, Trump administration working to hike them to 15 per cent
item.description: The United States began collecting a temporary new 10 per cent global import tariff on Tuesday but the Trump administration was working to increase it to 15 per cent, a White House official said, sowing confusion over President Donald Trump’s tariff policies in the wake of last week’s Supreme Court defeat.

item.title: Strong grain shipments by rail offset freight losses in 2025
item.description: Strong cereals volumes — particularly wheat — helped offset sharp declines in freight received from U.S. rail connections in 2025, with total freight moved by rail in Canada during the year down only marginally from 2024, Statistics Canada reported on Feb. 24.

item.title: UNDRIP appearing in agriculture sector’s radar
item.description: Federal government legislation, called the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, could affect future court decisions around public lands, major projects and resource development.

item.title: India and Canada to begin free trade talks during Carney’s visit, minister says
item.description: India hopes to start talks on a free trade agreement with Canada during Prime Minister Mark Carney’s visit to India later this week, the South Asian nation’s trade minister said on Tuesday.

item.title: Ag research will continue, federal minister says
item.description: Canada’s agriculture department plans to reduce its overhead by closing several research facilities, but still hopes to conduct as much ag research as before.

item.title: U.S. wheat sales to Indonesia about to rise significantly
item.description: U.S. wheat sales to Indonesia are set to rise following a trade agreement between the two countries, but not necessarily at the expense of Canadian wheat.

item.title: Consultations open on expanded regulations for drone pesticide application
item.description: Health Canada is seeking public opinion on proposed rules that would allow pesticides to be applied by drone if the chemicals are already registered for aerial application.

item.title: Mosaic misses profit estimates on weak U.S. phosphate demand
item.description: Mosaic missed Wall Street expectations for fourth-quarter profit on Tuesday, hurt by a steep drop in U.S. phosphate fertilizer demand that weighed on sales volumes.
